basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 32.' and it opens 'Vers. 32. Balaach filius Beor. Non est hic Balaach qui in libro Numerorum legitur mercede'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 32. Balaach filius Beor. Non est hic Balaach qui in libro Numerorum legitur mercede conduxisse Balaam ariolum. Ille enim rex fuit Edom, | iste vero rex fuit in Seir, et ille filius fuit Sephor, iste filius Beor.
